messages:
Anya: Quick heads-up — ran a full nsys + perfetto pass on the streaming path for a 2k-token request. Results look noisy; kernel selection keeps flipping between two matmul kernels mid-stream.
Devon: flipping how? different kernel IDs or different launch params?
Anya: different kernel names. Timeline shows `matmul_fused_v1` then `matmul_fused_v2` on alternating iterations. latency spikes ~30ms when v2 wins.
Miguel: are we seeing that only under nsys, or in production traces too?
Anya: repro in prod sampling (perfetto traces) as well. But when I profile with nvprof the flip doesn't show — suspects: CUPTI/nsys interaction with driver version.
Devon: what nsys / driver combo did you use?
Anya: nsys 2023.4.1, CUDA driver 535.54, libcupti from 12.4 (packaged with system). Also tried nsight-systems GUI on my laptop.
Miguel: we had a similar regression in Feb — driver 535.x had a kernel selection fallback bug for certain blockDim heuristics. Did you capture kernel launch params? timeline has args.
Anya: yeah included attrs. Perfetto snippet:
```
# open perfetto ui with:
perfetto --query --out=/tmp/trace.pb
# or upload trace.pb to perfetto.cloud
```
Anya: Example launch line (from CUPTI callbacks):
```
kernel: matmul_fused_v2 grid=(64,1,1) block=(256,1,1) shared=12288
```
Devon: v2 uses more shared mem — could cause runtime to pick a different kernel based on sm information. But why would it alternate on identical inputs?
Anya: My hypothesis: CUPTI timestamps are delivered slightly delayed with nsys agent enabled, and our kernel selector has a race using `cudaOccupancyMaxPotentialBlockSize` results cached per-stream. The race leads to reading stale occupancy info and selecting wrong kernel.
Miguel: ah, there are known CUPTI callback ordering differences across nsys versions. If CUptiActivityMemcpyX starts arriving before the kernel launch activity finishes, our heuristics mis-evaluate.
Devon: concrete repro steps? we should be able to reproduce locally with a smaller run.
Anya: Repro script attached in the trace (see root). Steps condensed:
1) build runtime with `-DPROFILING=1`
2) run nsys profile: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --output=out  ./serve --profile-run 200`
3) open `out.qdrep` in nsight or convert to `out.sqlite` and load into perfetto
Note: set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` and run as root on our test node else CUPTI permissions will drop frames.
Miguel: Permissions — we've seen `cupti` require read access to `/var/run/nv_peer_mem`? also mods for containers: need `--cap-add=SYS_ADMIN` sometimes.
Anya: yup, on the k8s node we had to add `privileged: true` to the debug pod to get full CUPTI capture. Without it we get truncated activity buffers.
Devon: ops-bot — did we recently upgrade nsys on the perf nodes?
ops-bot: Recent change: nsight-systems upgraded from 2022.5.x to 2023.4.1 on perf-nodes-3 two weeks ago. Rollback is possible if needed.
sre-bot: Noted: open an incident if this affects SLAs. Current traces show ~0.8% p50 regression for streaming path during deploy window.
Miguel: Two follow-ups: (A) validate with nsys 2022.5 to see if flip disappears, (B) add extra sync in kernel selector to avoid reading occupancy cache while CUPTI is active.
Anya: I tried downgrade locally to 2022.5 — flip gone. Also nvprof (deprecated) didn't show the issue because it doesn't interpose same CUPTI hooks.
Devon: Ok plan: schedule perf node rollback to 2022.5 for the week, put a feature flag to force stable kernel choice (cheap sync) in runtime. Then re-run perf baseline.
Miguel: also let's capture micro traces: enable `CUPTI_ENABLE=1 CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL=1` and dump raw CUPTI events — want to see arrival ordering.
Anya: I'll open a PR with the sync patch and attach the nsys + perfetto traces + a short script to reproduce. I'll also note required container capabilities in docs.
Devon: thanks — please include exact nsys command + driver version in the PR. Add a TODO to test on driver 540.x when available.
Anya: will do. tagging @Miguel for review and @Devon for rollout plan. :thumbsup:
